title: When the Extraction Burns
premise: Felix Lockridge, a ghost interpreter who handles deniable work for a fracturing peace delegation, receives a call on a burner phone from her presumed-dead brother, whose voice is being used as bait by someone inside the negotiation itself. Following the signal through three capitals, she uncovers that the peace talks are a cover for an arms pipeline sanctioned at the highest levels, and that the assassin hunting the delegation's witnesses is the one person she once loved. To expose the truth before the checkpoint shifts change and the evidence crosses into protected territory, Felix must choose between the duty that made her invisible and the loyalty that could get everyone killed. In the end she burns her own cover to put the truth on the record, lets the assassin walk into a trap of his own making, and walks away unnamed—alive, disavowed, and finally free.
about_author: Ulyana Winterbourne is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working behind glass in rooms where the real sentences were never the ones spoken aloud. She writes thrillers about people whose professions require them to be unheard.

chapters.title: The Language Nobody Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Working a failed pre-talk in a border city, Felix translates a delegation's polite lies while noting what everyone actually means. She establishes her rules: no names, no records, no attachments. Emotional beat: competent isolation—the comfort and cost of being nobody.

chapters.title: A Ring at the Wrong Hour
chapters.summary: POV Felix. A burner phone sewn into her coat lining rings; the voice is her brother Tomas, dead two years. He gives her a checkpoint time and hangs up. Emotional beat: grief weaponized—hope arriving in the shape of a trap.

chapters.title: Chain of Custody
chapters.summary: POV Felix. She traces the phone's purchase through a pawnshop and a dead courier, learning it was planted on her deliberately. Someone wants her moving. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Delegation's Quiet Man
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Deputy head of mission Aldous Vane recruits her for off-record interpretation with a foreign minister—work 'no one wants attributed.' She recognizes the phrasing: the same words used by whoever built the burner. Emotional beat: suspicion wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: What the Minister Meant
chapters.summary: POV Felix. During the session, Felix catches a coded phrase confirming arms shipments disguised as aid convoys. She memorizes rather than records. Emotional beat: the first irreversible knowledge—truth as burden.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Nine
chapters.summary: POV Felix. She stakes out Checkpoint Nine at shift change and sees the convoy pattern match the coded phrase—and sees the assassin, calm and familiar, overseeing it. Emotional beat: love and dread colliding in a single face.

chapters.title: Marek
chapters.summary: POV Felix, flashback-woven. Marek Sova, the man she loved and lost when an operation went wrong, is alive, employed, and killing witnesses. She reconstructs their history and how he faked his death. Emotional beat: betrayal reframing every memory she owns.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Cross-referencing leaked manifests, she maps how all three governments share the pipeline and need the peace talks to fail on schedule. Emotional beat: vertigo—the scale of the conspiracy swallowing her small truths.

chapters.title: The Second Call
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The burner rings again: not Tomas's voice this time but Marek's, warning her off with terrifying tenderness. He knows exactly where she sleeps. Emotional beat: intimacy as threat.

chapters.title: Borrowed Allegiance
chapters.summary: POV Felix. She approaches Inspector Dana Reyes, an honest cop inside a compromised service, and offers partial truth to build an alliance. Reyes tests her brutally. Emotional beat: trust negotiated like currency.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Talked
chapters.summary: POV Reyes. A logistics clerk willing to testify is found dead in a locked room staged as suicide. Reyes shares the file with Felix off the books. Emotional beat: grief hardening into shared resolve.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol, Personal Edition
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Vane offers Felix permanent protection if she translates the summit's closing statement—effectively making her complicit in burying the evidence. Emotional beat: temptation of safety priced in silence.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Living Hand
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Following Tomas's checkpoint clue, she retrieves a hidden drive containing the full pipeline ledger—Tomas was the courier, killed for it. Emotional beat: mourning converted to mission.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV Marek. Inside the assassin's discipline, we see him ordered to kill Felix and begin planning how to disobey without dying for it. Emotional beat: duty cracking under old love.

chapters.title: The Border Shifts at Midnight
chapters.summary: POV Felix. She learns the evidence must cross Checkpoint Nine before the 00:00 shift change, after which it enters diplomatic immunity and vanishes forever. The clock starts. Emotional beat: deadline as heartbeat.

chapters.title: House of Mirrors
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Vane reveals he knows about the drive and offers a trade: the drive for Tomas's killer's name—a name that points at Marek's handler, not Marek. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made literal.

chapters.title: Confession at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: POV Marek. Marek corners Felix to take the drive; instead they finally say everything unsaid. He gives her the handler's location and one hour's head start before reporting her. Emotional beat: love choosing sides at last.

chapters.title: The Long Hour
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Racing checkpoints and roadblocks, Felix delivers copies of the ledger to Reyes and a foreign journalist while evading both services. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into clarity.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Nine, 23:41
chapters.summary: POV Felix and Marek alternating. At the final crossing, Marek turns on his handler to buy Felix the minutes she needs; the confrontation turns lethal. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the only honest translation left.

chapters.title: What Burns
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The handler is captured, the ledger goes public mid-summit, and the talks collapse into scandal instead of signature. Vane falls; the machine grinds but is seen. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, imperfect and real.

chapters.title: After the Signature That Never Came
chapters.summary: POV Reyes. The fallout: inquiries open, careers end, Felix officially never existed. Reyes burns her file as a gift. Emotional beat: quiet vindication between two women who chose truth over institution.

chapters.title: Interpreter, Unemployed
chapters.summary: POV Felix. At a border café near Checkpoint Nine, Felix answers a call on the burner—Tomas's voice again, or perhaps just the wind. She smiles, pockets the phone, and walks toward the crossing. Emotional beat: open-hearted ambiguity; invisibility chosen, not imposed.
